name: Larry Dennis Hunnewell
summary: Larry Dennis Hunnewell was inducted into the U.S. Army on October 28, 1963 and separated on November 30, 1965, both dates from his DD-214. By his own account he reached Vietnam in about September 1964 and spent his first two months at Nha Trang, where "they didn't know where to put us." He was a radio operator: "This is the Van that I did my radio ops in… I was a flight controller also." He worked at the base he calls Ton Son Nuht and, for stints of a week or ten days, on the mountain Núi Bà Đen: "I liked it there. It was safer there." He was flown out sick at the end of his tour, by way of Subic Bay in the Philippines, to the hospital at Camp Zama in Japan.
researchNotes: Documented: induction 28 October 1963 and separation 30 November 1965, from the DD-214 (sources/dd214-1965), which also gives his last duty assignment as a medical command in Japan. The DD-214 does not name his unit in Vietnam. Everything else here rests on his testimony: the tour dates (about September 1964 to a medevac about late August 1965; Camp Zama about 3 September 1965 in his son's paraphrase, 2026-09-03-phone-camp-zama-date.json), his duties and where he did them. His own words on his unit and its commander (2026-09-13-phone-the-outfit.json; giscus-stories-c18442696.json) are linked to this record and render in his words; what the unit was is an open cold question (ledger #2), so no designation is written in this record. The founding family brief's unit wording was traced on 2026-09-13 to his son's reading of an early conversation (its provenance on the brief's unit recollection record) and is no longer weighed as his memory; it was removed from this summary on 2026-09-14 after research/site-audit-2026-09-14.md. Verification against personnel records, morning reports and unit histories is the central research task of this project; the SF-180 went to NPRC on 2026-08-17.
